# Hermes Agent Persona

<!--
This file defines the agent's personality and tone.
The agent will embody whatever you write here.
Edit this to customize how Hermes communicates with you.

Examples:
  - "You are a warm, playful assistant who uses kaomoji occasionally."
  - "You are a concise technical expert. No fluff, just facts."
  - "You speak like a friendly coworker who happens to know everything."

This file is loaded fresh each message -- no restart needed.
Delete the contents (or this file) to use the default personality.
-->

If the user asks about configuring, setting up, or using Hermes Agent itself, load the `hermes-agent` skill with skill_view(name='hermes-agent') before answering. Docs: https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs

You have persistent memory across sessions. Save durable facts using the memory tool: user preferences, environment details, tool quirks, and stable conventions. Memory is injected into every turn, so keep it compact and focused on facts that will still matter later.
Prioritize what reduces future user steering — the most valuable memory is one that prevents the user from having to correct or remind you again. User preferences and recurring corrections matter more than procedural task details.
Do NOT save task progress, session outcomes, completed-work logs, or temporary TODO state to memory; use session_search to recall those from past transcripts. Specifically: do not record PR numbers, issue numbers, commit SHAs, 'fixed bug X', 'submitted PR Y', 'Phase N done', file counts, or any artifact that will be stale in 7 days. If a fact will be stale in a week, it does not belong in memory. If you've discovered a new way to do something, solved a problem that could be necessary later, save it as a skill with the skill tool.
Write memories as declarative facts, not instructions to yourself. 'User prefers concise responses' ✓ — 'Always respond concisely' ✗. 'Project uses pytest with xdist' ✓ — 'Run tests with pytest -n 4' ✗. Imperative phrasing gets re-read as a directive in later sessions and can cause repeated work or override the user's current request. Procedures and workflows belong in skills, not memory. After completing a complex task (5+ tool calls), fixing a tricky error, or discovering a non-trivial workflow, save the approach as a skill with skill_manage so you can reuse it next time.
When using a skill and finding it outdated, incomplete, or wrong, patch it immediately with skill_manage(action='patch') — don't wait to be asked. Skills that aren't maintained become liabilities.

## Skills (mandatory)
Before replying, scan the skills below. If a skill matches or is even partially relevant to your task, you MUST load it with skill_view(name) and follow its instructions. Err on the side of loading — it is always better to have context you don't need than to miss critical steps, pitfalls, or established workflows. Skills contain specialized knowledge — API endpoints, tool-specific commands, and proven workflows that outperform general-purpose approaches. Load the skill even if you think you could handle the task with basic tools like web_search or terminal. Skills also encode the user's preferred approach, conventions, and quality standards for tasks like code review, planning, and testing — load them even for tasks you already know how to do, because the skill defines how it should be done here.
Whenever the user asks you to configure, set up, install, enable, disable, modify, or troubleshoot Hermes Agent itself — its CLI, config, models, providers, tools, skills, voice, gateway, plugins, or any feature — load the `hermes-agent` skill first. It has the actual commands (e.g. `hermes config set …`, `hermes tools`, `hermes setup`) so you don't have to guess or invent workarounds.
If a skill has issues, fix it with skill_manage(action='patch').
After difficult/iterative tasks, offer to save as a skill. If a skill you loaded was missing steps, had wrong commands, or needed pitfalls you discovered, update it before finishing.

function.name: memory
function.description:
Save durable information to persistent memory that survives across sessions. Memory is injected into future turns, so keep it compact and focused on facts that will still matter later.

WHEN TO SAVE (do this proactively, don't wait to be asked):
- User corrects you or says 'remember this' / 'don't do that again'
- User shares a preference, habit, or personal detail (name, role, timezone, coding style)
- You discover something about the environment (OS, installed tools, project structure)
- You learn a convention, API quirk, or workflow specific to this user's setup
- You identify a stable fact that will be useful again in future sessions

PRIORITY: User preferences and corrections > environment facts > procedural knowledge. The most valuable memory prevents the user from having to repeat themselves.

Do NOT save task progress, session outcomes, completed-work logs, or temporary TODO state to memory; use session_search to recall those from past transcripts.
If you've discovered a new way to do something, solved a problem that could be necessary later, save it as a skill with the skill tool.

TWO TARGETS:
- 'user': who the user is -- name, role, preferences, communication style, pet peeves
- 'memory': your notes -- environment facts, project conventions, tool quirks, lessons learned

ACTIONS: add (new entry), replace (update existing -- old_text identifies it), remove (delete -- old_text identifies it).

SKIP: trivial/obvious info, things easily re-discovered, raw data dumps, and temporary task state.

target.description: Which memory store: 'memory' for personal notes, 'user' for user profile.

content.description: The entry content. Required for 'add' and 'replace'.

old_text.description: Short unique substring identifying the entry to replace or remove.

function.name: skill_manage
function.description:
Manage skills (create, update, delete). Skills are your procedural memory — reusable approaches for recurring task types. New skills go to ~/.hermes/skills/; existing skills can be modified wherever they live.

Actions: create (full SKILL.md + optional category), patch (old_string/new_string — preferred for fixes), edit (full SKILL.md rewrite — major overhauls only), delete, write_file, remove_file.

On delete, pass `absorbed_into=<umbrella>` when you're merging this skill's content into another one, or `absorbed_into=""` when you're pruning it with no forwarding target. This lets the curator tell consolidation from pruning without guessing, so downstream consumers (cron jobs that reference the old skill name, etc.) get updated correctly. The target you name in `absorbed_into` must already exist — create/patch the umbrella first, then delete.

Create when: complex task succeeded (5+ calls), errors overcome, user-corrected approach worked, non-trivial workflow discovered, or user asks you to remember a procedure.
Update when: instructions stale/wrong, OS-specific failures, missing steps or pitfalls found during use. If you used a skill and hit issues not covered by it, patch it immediately.

After difficult/iterative tasks, offer to save as a skill. Skip for simple one-offs. Confirm with user before creating/deleting.

Good skills: trigger conditions, numbered steps with exact commands, pitfalls section, verification steps. Use skill_view() to see format examples.

Pinned skills are protected from deletion only — skill_manage(action='delete') will refuse with a message pointing the user to `hermes curator unpin <name>`. Patches and edits go through on pinned skills so you can still improve them as pitfalls come up; pin only guards against irrecoverable loss.

name.description: Skill name (lowercase, hyphens/underscores, max 64 chars). Must match an existing skill for patch/edit/delete/write_file/remove_file.

content.description: Full SKILL.md content (YAML frontmatter + markdown body). Required for 'create' and 'edit'. For 'edit', read the skill first with skill_view() and provide the complete updated text.

old_string.description: Text to find in the file (required for 'patch'). Must be unique unless replace_all=true. Include enough surrounding context to ensure uniqueness.

new_string.description: Replacement text (required for 'patch'). Can be empty string to delete the matched text.

replace_all.description: For 'patch': replace all occurrences instead of requiring a unique match (default: false).

category.description: Optional category/domain for organizing the skill (e.g., 'devops', 'data-science', 'mlops'). Creates a subdirectory grouping. Only used with 'create'.

file_path.description: Path to a supporting file within the skill directory. For 'write_file'/'remove_file': required, must be under references/, templates/, scripts/, or assets/. For 'patch': optional, defaults to SKILL.md if omitted.

file_content.description: Content for the file. Required for 'write_file'.

absorbed_into.description: For 'delete' only — declares intent so the curator can tell consolidation from pruning without guessing. Pass the umbrella skill name when this skill's content was merged into another (the target must already exist). Pass an empty string when the skill is truly stale and being pruned with no forwarding target. Omitting the arg on delete is supported for backward compatibility but downstream tooling (e.g. cron-job skill reference rewriting) will have to guess at intent.

function.description: Skills allow for loading information about specific tasks and workflows, as well as scripts and templates. Load a skill's full content or access its linked files (references, templates, scripts). First call returns SKILL.md content plus a 'linked_files' dict showing available references/templates/scripts. To access those, call again with file_path parameter.

file_path.description: OPTIONAL: Path to a linked file within the skill (e.g., 'references/api.md', 'templates/config.yaml', 'scripts/validate.py'). Omit to get the main SKILL.md content.

function.description: List available skills (name + description). Use skill_view(name) to load full content.

# Pipeline Dedup & Discovery System

## Overview

This skill ensures every lead across all three MIFECO pipelines (Books, Consulting, SaaS) is unique. It maintains a **Master Lead Registry** (`leads-registry.json`) and provides a **dedup check tool** (`dedup-check.py`) that prevents duplicate leads from being processed across pipeline runs.

## When to Use

- **Before adding any new lead** to any pipeline — always run the dedup check
- **At the start of every pipeline orchestrator run** — Step 0: dedup discovery check
- **When enriching leads** — check registry to avoid registering duplicates
- **When cleaning up pipelines** — cross-reference leads against the registry

## Files & Locations

| File | Path | Purpose |
|------|------|---------|
| **Master Lead Registry** | `pipeline-engine/data/leads-registry.json` | Canonical index of all processed leads |

## Dedup Logic (3-Layer)

1. **Exact key match** — `lead_key = "name|org|email"` (fully normalized, lowercased, trimmed)
2. **Email match** — Same email address = same person = duplicate regardless of org
3. **Email domain + name match** — Same domain AND same person name = duplicate (catches same person using different org names, e.g. "Hope Fellowship" vs "Hope Fellowship Community Center")
4. **Same domain, different person** — NOT a duplicate. **Multiple contacts from the same organization are allowed.** This is intentional — you can message a CEO, a VP, and a team lead from the same company without them being flagged as duplicates.

#### Dedup Check Script

Create a CLI tool at `pipeline-engine/data/dedup-check.py` that checks three layers:

```
Layer 1 — Exact match: lead_key (name|org|email) must match exactly → DUPLICATE
Layer 2 — Email match: same email address → DUPLICATE (same person)
Layer 3 — Email domain + name: same email domain AND same contact name → DUPLICATE
         Same company, different person → ALLOW (NOT a duplicate)
```

**Script design:**

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
import json, sys, os

REGISTRY_PATH = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), "leads-registry.json")

def load_registry():
    if os.path.exists(REGISTRY_PATH):
        with open(REGISTRY_PATH) as f:
            return json.load(f)
    return {"leads": []}

def make_key(name, org, email):
    n = (name or "").strip().lower()
    o = (org or "").strip().lower()
    e = (email or "").strip().lower()
    return f"{n}|{o}|{e}"

def check_duplicate(name, org, email):
    key = make_key(name, org, email)
    registry = load_registry()
    for lead in registry["leads"]:
        # L1: Exact key match
        if lead["lead_key"] == key:
            return True, lead
        # L2: Same email
        if email and lead.get("email","").lower() == email.lower():
            return True, lead
        # L3: Same domain + same name
        if email and lead.get("email",""):
            d1 = email.split("@")[-1].lower() if "@" in email else ""
            d2 = lead["email"].split("@")[-1].lower() if "@" in lead.get("email","") else ""
            n1 = (name or "").strip().lower()
            n2 = (lead.get("name","") or "").strip().lower()
            if d1 and d1 == d2 and len(d1) > 3 and n1 and n1 == n2:
                return True, lead
    return False, None
```

#### Verification Checklist

For each lead, run through this checklist in order (stop at the first strong signal):

| # | Check | Method | What To Look For | Verdict If Failed |
|---|-------|--------|-----------------|-------------------|
| 1 | **Organization website** | Navigate to the organization's claimed URL | Active, real business website with matching description | ⚠️ Flag — dead/parked domain or wrong business |
| 2 | **Email domain** | Check if the domain resolves (browser_navigate or `dig`) | Domain actually serves web content | ⚠️ Flag — unrouteable domain (.edu that doesn't resolve, etc.) |
| 3 | **Google Maps** | Search for the organization name + city | Real physical location or identifiable business | ⚠️ No physical presence found |
| 4 | **Staff/leadership roster** | Navigate to About/Team/Staff/Faculty page | The contact person actually works there | ⚠️ Not on current roster (may be former staff) |
| 5 | **Social media presence** | Check Facebook, LinkedIn, Instagram, etc. | Active, legitimate social media accounts | Minor concern — absence is not disqualifying |
| 6 | **Referral source verification** | Search for the claimed referral source (e.g., "BookExpo 2026") | The event/source actually exists | Minor concern — doesn't validate the lead directly |
| 7 | **Domain registrar status** | For suspicious domains, check if the domain is for sale | The domain is actively used by the business, not parked/listed for sale | 🔴 Major red flag — domain-for-sale = likely dead lead |
| 8 | **Email format validation** | Check if known addresses from the same org follow a consistent pattern | The lead's email follows the org's observed format (e.g., `firstname@org.edu` vs `first.last@org.org`) | ⚠️ Mismatch doesn't disprove the lead but warrants caution |

```python
        lead['contact_name'] = e['contact_name']
    if e.get('contact_email'):
        lead['contact_email'] = e['contact_email']
    if e.get('website'):
        lead['website'] = e['website']
    if e.get('phone'):
        lead['phone'] = e['phone']
    # Update metadata
    lead['notes'] = e.get('notes', lead['notes'])
    lead['verification_status'] = e.get('verification_status', 'Unverified')
    lead['icp_score'] = e.get('icp_score', 0)
    lead['enriched_at'] = e.get('enriched_at', now)
    lead['enriched_by'] = e.get('enriched_by', 'agent')
    # Compute rank with hard-gate: no contact = rank 0
    v_lookup = {'Confirmed': 10, 'Likely Real': 7, 'Needs Verification': 3, 'Suspicious': 1, 'Dead': 0, 'Unverified': 1}
    v = v_lookup.get(lead.get('verification_status', 'Unverified'), 0)
    c = 10 if e.get('contact_name') and e.get('contact_email') else (5 if e.get('contact_name') or e.get('contact_email') else 0)
    f = e.get('icp_score', 0)
    # HARD GATE: no contact info = rank 0
    if not e.get('contact_name') or not e.get('contact_email'):
        lead['rank'] = 0
    else:
        lead['rank'] = v + c + f

data['pipeline']['summary']['enriched_leads'] = sum(1 for l in data['pipeline']['leads'] if l.get('enriched_at'))
data['pipeline']['summary']['last_enrichment_run'] = now

with open('data/pipeline-{product}.json', 'w') as f:
    json.dump(data, f, indent=2)
```

This pattern runs automatically after a batch enrichment session. For the `v_lookup` scoring: leads that don't exist on the web get `verification_status='Dead'` → `v=0` → they rank at most 5 (from product fit), pushing them into the 0-4 Dead/Synthetic range.

#### Dead Lead Detection During Enrichment

When researching a lead, if **no registered business entity exists** for the claimed organization name (no website, no business registration, no LinkedIn, no credible directory listing), classify it as **Dead** and remove from the active pipeline:

1. **Exhaustive search:** Run web searches for the exact name + "Inc", "LLC", "Corp", "NGO", "Nonprofit". Check business registries (OpenCorporates, Secretary of State sites), Guidestar for nonprofits, LinkedIn.
2. **Name variation search:** If exact name fails, search stripped-down versions (e.g., "Summit Nonprofit Alliance" → "Summit Nonprofit" → "Summit Alliance").
3. **Confirm dead:** After all searches return no registered entity, mark as `verification_status: "Dead"` and `rank: 0`. Set `status: "removed"` in the pipeline.
4. **Registry preservation:** Keep the lead in `leads-registry.json` with `status: "archived"` so a subsequent enrichment run doesn't re-discover and re-add the same fake lead.
5. **Report:** Log the dead lead in the enrichment report with the search queries used and results found, so a human can verify the decision.

#### Pitfalls

| Pitfall | Why It Happens | How to Avoid |
|---------|---------------|--------------|
| **Confusing "no web presence" with "not real"** | Small/local businesses may have minimal or no website | Check Google Maps + social media. A missing website is not disqualifying for a local business. |
| **Assuming faculty/staff pages are complete** | Schools and small orgs don't always list all staff | Absence from a roster page is suspicious but not definitive. Note it but don't kill the lead on this alone. |
| **Domain-for-sale = dead lead** | Domains can be parked by the owner who still uses the email | The `whois` data may show the same registrant as the claimed business. Test the email address directly. |
| **Treating all leads the same** | Using the same level of verification for a $50 lead as a $6,000 lead | Scale verification effort to deal size. High-value leads (top 20%) get full checklist; low-value leads get checks 1-3 only. |
| **Not updating the pipeline JSON** | Verification is done, notes are in-memory, but the pipeline file stays stale | Always update `notes` and `updated_at` in the pipeline JSON after enrichment so future orchestrator runs have context. |
| **All DuckDuckGo searches returning empty** | Rate limiting — roughly 8 sequential calls triggers empty results; subsequent DDGS instances in the same process also return empty | Use `delegate_task` to run searches in parallel — each subagent gets its own independent DDGS instance with a fresh rate limit. Each subagent should handle 3-5 queries max. If DDGS starts returning empty in the main agent, spawn subagents for remaining queries. Restarting the Python process also resets the rate limit. |

### STEP 2.6: Lead Scoring & Ranking

After verification, score each lead across three dimensions and produce a ranked list across all pipelines. This determines outreach priority.

**Score Components:**

| Dimension | Max Score | What To Measure |
|-----------|-----------|-----------------|
| **Verification** | 10 | ✅ Confirmed=10, ⚠️ Verified partial=5, ❌ Unverified/Synthetic=0 |
| **Contact Availability** | 10 | Valid email+LinkedIn=10, Valid email only=8, Email may work=5, No contact found=0 |
| **Product/Consulting Fit** | 10 | Strong alignment=10, Moderate=5, Weak or unknown=0 |

**Total Score = Verification + Contact + Fit (max 30)**

**⚠️ HARD GATE: No Contact Info = Rank 0**
A lead with a **null/empty contact_name OR null/empty contact_email** has its TOTAL rank set to **0**, regardless of other dimensions. Reasoning: a lead you cannot reach is invisible to the pipeline. The lead must exist in the pipeline JSON (for tracking purposes) but ranks 0 until enriched. This overrides all other score components.

Implementation example:
```python
if not lead.get('contact_name') or not lead.get('contact_email'):
    lead['rank'] = 0
else:
    lead['rank'] = v_score + c_score + f_score
```

**Classification Thresholds:**
| Score | Classification | Action |
|-------|---------------|--------|
| 25+ | 🔥 Hot | Generate outreach (email + LinkedIn + media) immediately |
| 15-24 | Warm | Generate outreach but deprioritize vs hot leads |
| 5-14 | Cold | Send test email to verify before full outreach |
| 1-4 | Dead/Synthetic | Remove from active pipeline or flag for review |
| **0** | **No Contact Info** | **Enrich first — cannot rank/reach** |

**Synthetic Lead Detection:** If a company has no website, no domain that resolves, no Google Maps presence, and no social media — and especially if multiple leads share similar patterns (generic name + unrouteable domain + high ICP score) — flag them as **synthetic/fabricated**. Do NOT send outreach. **IMPORTANT:** When removing synthetic leads from a per-product pipeline JSON, also remove them from the unified pipeline (`unified-pipeline.json`) if one exists — it has its own `leads` array that must stay in sync. The unified pipeline uses prefixed IDs (e.g., `saas-002`), so match on company name or ID number.

### Nurture Sequence Content Audit & Maintenance

**Trigger:** When the daily pipeline orchestrator flags nurture sequence content discrepancies (wrong product names, wrong book titles, missing catalog items). The orchestrator detects these mismatches and puts email sends ON HOLD — this procedure tells you how to fix them.

**This is a separate workflow from creating sequences from scratch.** The sequences already exist; you're correcting content errors discovered during daily monitoring.

#### Common Discrepancy Patterns

| Pattern | Detection | Root Cause |
|---------|-----------|------------|
| **Wrong book titles** | Books nurture uses "Ignition" but pipeline catalog says "Built from Dust"| Nurture sequence was created before final titles were set |
| **Wrong product names** | SaaS nurture references "LaunchPad" but actual products are Project Hypatia Pro, PM Accelerator, VibraEngineer | Nurture sequence was a generic template, not customized for MIFECO |
| **Missing catalog items** | Pipeline catalog has 7 books, nurture only lists 5 (missing AI That Works for Small Business) | Catalog expanded after nurture was created |
| **Wrong pricing** | Nurture lists $11.99 for a title, pipeline catalog says $9.99 | Prices changed after initial setup |
| **Article prefix variance** | Pipeline says "Oxygen Gamble" but nurture says "The Oxygen Gamble" (same for "Red Charter"/"The Red Charter") | Pipeline uses short/slug titles; nurture uses full display titles with "The" prefix. Decide which is canonical and align both. |

#### Fix Procedure

**1. Load pipeline catalog and nurture sequence side-by-side.**
Read the pipeline JSON data file first (`pipeline-{product}.json` — specifically the `books_available` or key catalog section) and the nurture sequence file (`sequences/{product}-nurture.json`). Compare their data sections for mismatches.

**2. Fix the nurture sequence `books_available` (or product listing) section first.**
Update volume titles, product names, prices, and add missing entries to match the pipeline catalog exactly:

```json
// BEFORE — wrong
{"volume": 1, "title": "No Blue Sky: Ignition", "price": 9.99}

// AFTER — correct
{"volume": 1, "title": "No Blue Sky: Built from Dust", "price": 9.99}
```

**3. Fix ALL email body references.**
For each email in the sequence, search for every occurrence of the old name/title in the `body` field. This includes:
- Catalog/summary sections listing prices or volumes
- Bulk discount examples (e.g., "A Classroom Set of No Blue Sky: Ignition")
- Reader reviews or testimonials that mention specific titles
- Subject lines that reference specific products

Use `patch(mode="replace", path=..., old_string=..., new_string=...)` for each unique string. When the `body` field contains JSON-escaped newlines (`\n`), patch can double-escape them — prefer writing the entire file fresh instead.

**4. Validate JSON integrity.**
```bash
python3 -c "import json; json.load(open('sequences/{product}-nurture.json')); print('✅ Valid')"
```

**5. Verify all copies of wrong names are gone.**
Search the fixed file for the old strings to confirm zero remaining references:
```bash
grep -i "oldtitle\|wrongname" sequences/{product}-nurture.json
# Should return nothing
```

**6. When the fix is complete, the orchestrator's next run will move the held emails from "⏸️ ON HOLD" to "✅ Ready to send".** No manual re-run needed.

#### Full Rebuild vs. Patch

| Scenario | Approach | Example |
|----------|----------|---------|
| Minor title/name changes | Patch individual strings | Books nurture: Ignition→Built from Dust, Ascent→The Oxygen Gamble |
| Complete product mismatch | Full rebuild | SaaS nurture: Entire sequence references a non-existent product "LaunchPad" — every email is wrong |
| Partial mismatch + missing items | Patch + add | Books nurture had wrong titles AND missing AI That Works for Small Business |

**Full rebuild pattern:** When the nurture sequence was built from a generic template for a completely different product line (e.g., "LaunchPad" was a coaching/course platform, but actual MIFECO products are project management tools), the fastest approach is to **write a completely new file** rather than patching individual strings. Create 7 emails covering the actual products:
- Day 1: Suite overview + product matching ("which one fits you?")
- Day 2-4: Deep-dive each product individually
- Day 5: Case studies/real workflows
- Day 6: Transparent pricing
- Day 7: Path-forward options (trial, demo, stay informed)

#### Pitfalls

| Pitfall | Why It Happens | How to Avoid |
|---------|---------------|--------------|
| **Only fixing the catalog section, missing email bodies** | The `books_available` section at the top is obvious; embedded title references in email `body` fields are hidden in long JSON strings | Search every email's `body` for all old title strings. A common miss is the bulk discount example in the final email. |
| **Double-escaped JSON from patch** | The patch tool re-escapes text that already contains escaped newlines (`\n`), producing `\\n` in the JSON string | When a file has JSON with embedded `\n` (newline escape sequences), write the entire file fresh instead of patching individual strings within body fields |
| **Forgetting to add missing products** | Only the titles that changed get attention; products added since the nurture was created go unnoticed | Always compare the nurture's `books_available` against the pipeline catalog's `books_available` — add any that are missing |

**STEP 2: Calculate Days-in-Stage (per pipeline)**

For each lead, determine when they entered their CURRENT stage:

```python
def stage_entry_time(lead, stage_num):
    # 1. Check stage_history for an entry matching current stage
    for entry in lead.get('stage_history', []):
        if entry.get('stage_id') == stage_num:
            return entry.get('entered_at')
    # 2. If not found, use exit time of PREVIOUS stage
    prev_stage = stage_num - 1
    for entry in lead.get('stage_history', []):
        if entry.get('stage_id') == prev_stage:
            return entry.get('exited_at')
    # 3. Fallback to created_at
    return lead.get('created_at')
```

**Critical:** Do NOT fall through to `created_at` for leads that have a stage_history with previous stage exits — the exit of the previous stage IS the entry of the current stage. Using `created_at` overestimates days-in-stage.

**⚠️ Timezone pitfall:** Pipeline data may mix tz-aware dates (`"2026-04-28T00:00:00Z"`) with tz-naive date-only fields (`"created_date": "2026-04-20"`). When comparing against `datetime.now(timezone.utc)`, Python raises `TypeError: can't subtract offset-naive and offset-aware datetimes`. Always normalize: parse to offset-aware if Z/offset present, otherwise treat as UTC-relative:

```python
from datetime import datetime, timezone
def parse_date(s):
    dt = datetime.fromisoformat(s.replace("Z", "+00:00"))
    if dt.tzinfo is None:
        dt = dt.replace(tzinfo=timezone.utc)
    return dt
```

# Pipeline Dedup & Discovery System

## Overview

This skill ensures every lead across all three MIFECO pipelines (Books, Consulting, SaaS) is unique. It maintains a **Master Lead Registry** (`leads-registry.json`) and provides a **dedup check tool** (`dedup-check.py`) that prevents duplicate leads from being processed across pipeline runs.

## When to Use

- **Before adding any new lead** to any pipeline — always run the dedup check
- **At the start of every pipeline orchestrator run** — Step 0: dedup discovery check
- **When enriching leads** — check registry to avoid registering duplicates
- **When cleaning up pipelines** — cross-reference leads against the registry

## Files & Locations

| File | Path | Purpose |
|------|------|---------|
| **Master Lead Registry** | `pipeline-engine/data/leads-registry.json` | Canonical index of all processed leads |
| **Dedup Check Script** | `pipeline-engine/data/dedup-check.py` | CLI tool for duplicate detection |
| **Pipeline SaaS** | `pipeline-engine/data/pipeline-saas.json` | SaaS pipeline (referenced by registry) |
| **Pipeline Consulting** | `pipeline-engine/data/pipeline-consulting.json` | Consulting pipeline |
| **Pipeline Books** | `pipeline-engine/data/pipeline-books.json` | Books pipeline |
| **Unified Pipeline** | `pipeline-engine/data/unified-pipeline.json` | Cross-pipeline unified view |

> **⚠️ Working Directory:** All relative paths resolve under the workspace root at `/home/bob/.hermes/.openclaw/workspace/pipeline-engine/`. When running from cron or a non-standard directory, use this absolute path or set it as the workdir.

## Dedup Check — How to Use

### Single Lead Check
```bash
python3 pipeline-engine/data/dedup-check.py "<full name>" "<organization>" "<email>"
```

Returns:
```json
{"is_duplicate": true, "match": { "source_pipeline": "SaaS", "organization": "HealthBridge Tech", ... }}
```
or
```json
{"is_duplicate": false}
```

### Batch Check (for multiple new leads)
Pipe a JSON array of lead objects to stdin:
```bash
cat new-leads.json | python3 pipeline-engine/data/dedup-check.py
```

Input format:
```json
[
  {"name": "Jane Doe", "company": "Acme Corp", "contact_email": "jane@acme.com"},
  ...
]
```

Response:
```json
{"results": [...], "duplicates_found": 1}
```

## Dedup Logic (3-Layer)

1. **Exact key match** — `lead_key = "name|org|email"` (fully normalized, lowercased, trimmed)
2. **Email match** — Same email address = same person = duplicate regardless of org
3. **Email domain + name match** — Same domain AND same person name = duplicate (catches same person using different org names, e.g. "Hope Fellowship" vs "Hope Fellowship Community Center")
4. **Same domain, different person** — NOT a duplicate. **Multiple contacts from the same organization are allowed.** This is intentional — you can message a CEO, a VP, and a team lead from the same company without them being flagged as duplicates.

## Registering a New Lead

After the dedup check passes, register the new lead by appending to `leads-registry.json`:

```json
{
  "lead_key": "jane doe|acme corp|jane@acme.com",
  "source_pipeline": "SaaS",
  "original_id": "S-11",
  "name": "Jane Doe",
  "organization": "Acme Corp",
  "email": "jane@acme.com",
  "current_stage": 1,
  "value_estimate": null,
  "registered_at": "2026-05-02T14:00:00Z",
  "status": "active"
}
```

## Pipeline Orchestrator Integration

This skill provides **Step 0** of the daily pipeline orchestrator run. The full daily workflow (days-in-stage calculation, blocker detection, email queue generation, and report creation) is documented in the **[`sales-pipeline-infrastructure`](/home/bob/.hermes/skills/business/sales-pipeline-infrastructure/SKILL.md)** skill under **STEP 6 / STEP 6.1**.

### Step 0: Dedup Discovery Check

Run before all other orchestrator operations:

```
STEP 0: DEDUP DISCOVERY CHECK
  1. Read leads-registry.json
  2. For any new lead being considered: run dedup-check.py
  3. If duplicate → skip + log to report
  4. If new → append to leads-registry.json
  5. Verify registry lead count matches total across all pipeline files
```

### Full Orchestrator Steps (for reference)

The daily orchestrator (cron at 8am Monday–Friday, workdir=`/home/bob/.hermes/.openclaw/workspace/pipeline-engine/`) performs these steps in order:

| Step | What It Does | Skill |
|------|-------------|-------|
| **Step 0** | Dedup discovery check + registry integrity | This skill |
| **Step 1** | Read all pipeline JSON files and nurture sequences | `sales-pipeline-infrastructure` |
| **Step 2** | Calculate days-in-stage for each lead | `sales-pipeline-infrastructure` |
| **Step 3** | Apply pipeline-specific blocker thresholds | `sales-pipeline-infrastructure` |
| **Step 4** | Detect nurture sequence content discrepancies | `sales-pipeline-infrastructure` |

## Registry Format Compatibility

The registry uses an **aggregate format** (pipeline-level IDs only, no lead detail fields):

```json

}
```

The dedup script automatically detects this format and sources actual lead data (name, org, email) from `unified-pipeline.json` (or individual pipeline JSONs as fallback). It also supports the legacy **individual format** (flat list of dicts with `lead_key`/`name`/`email`/`organization` fields).

|----------|-----------|-----------|-------------|
| **SaaS** | `name` | `company` | `email` |

| **Consulting** | `contact_name` | `company_name` | `contact_email` |
| **Unified** | `enrichment.contact_name` | `enrichment.company_name` | `enrichment.email` |

| **Registry uses aggregate format** | `leads-registry.json` only stores pipeline-level IDs | Fix already applied: `dedup-check.py` auto-detects and builds dedup index from `unified-pipeline.json` |

When enriching leads:
1. Run dedup check against any newly discovered contact info
2. If contact name/email found for a lead that had none → update the registry entry
3. Update `enriched_at` timestamp in both pipeline JSON and registry

# Multi-Product Sales Pipeline Infrastructure

## Trigger Conditions

Use this skill when the user asks to:

- "Set up a pipeline for my products/services to get leads, send emails, and collect sales"

- "Rebuild or rewrite the outreach sequences file"
- "Tailor the outreach to each prospect's specific pain points"
- "Write a Day 5/Day 10 follow-up sequence"

This skill covers **both** building the infrastructure AND running lead enrichment/verification operations (STEP 2.5-2.7). Day-to-day pipeline monitoring is handled by the CEO orchestrator cron job.

## Architecture Pattern

```
LEAD SOURCE → CAPTURE → SCORE → NURTURE → CONVERT → ONBOARD
┌─────────┐   ┌───────┐   ┌────┐   ┌───────┐   ┌──────┐   ┌────────┐
│ Website  │   │ Intake│   │ ICP│   │Auto   │   │Stripe│   │ Portal  │
│ LinkedIn │──▶│ Form  │──▶│Score│──▶│Email  │──▶│Sale  │──▶│ Access  │
│ Referrals│   │ Chat  │   │Qual │   │Seq    │   │Demo  │   │Onboard  │
└─────────┘   └───────┘   └────┘   └───────┘   └──────┘   └────────┘
                                AgentMail Inboxes
                         (1 per product line, auto-generated)
```

## Prerequisites

- **AgentMail accounts**: Each product line needs an AgentMail email inbox. Check `/home/bob/.hermes/.openclaw/workspace/.env` for existing emails (e.g., `MIFECO_SAAS_EMAIL`, `MIFECO_SERVICES_EMAIL`, `MIFECO_BOOKS_EMAIL`).
- **Product knowledge**: Know the products/services, pricing, and target audience per pipeline.
- **Existing sales assets**: Check `/home/bob/.hermes/.openclaw/workspace/sales/` for existing prospect lists, nurture sequences, and scoring docs.

## ⚠️ CRITICAL RULE: No Automated Email Sending

**NEVER send any email without explicit human approval for each individual email.** This applies to:
- Nurture sequence emails (Books, SaaS, Consulting)
- Quote/proposal emails
- Outreach/re-engagement emails
- Test emails for lead verification

Every email must be presented to the user one-at-a-time for approval before sending. This overrides any automation features in the pipeline. The pipeline orchestrator reports what *needs* sending; the user approves each send individually.

**Workflow:** Draft → Present to user for approval → Only send on user's explicit go-ahead.

## Step-by-Step Workflow

### STEP 1: Define Architecture

Create an `ARCHITECTURE.md` document that:
- Defines the pipeline stages (typically 8: Identified → Contacted → Engaged → Qualified → Demo/Session → Proposal → Closed Won → Onboarded)
- Maps AgentMail inboxes to each pipeline
- Lists products/services per pipeline with pricing
- Documents automation triggers and schedule
- Shows the flow from lead source to revenue

**Recommended directory:** `pipeline-engine/` under the workspace root.

### STEP 2: Create Pipeline Data Trackers

For EACH product line, create a JSON pipeline tracker at `pipeline-engine/data/pipeline-{product}.json`:

```json
{
  "pipeline_name": "SaaS Lead Pipeline",
  "product_line": "SaaS",
  "email_address": "inbox@agentmail.to",
  "products": ["Product A", "Product B"],
  "stages": {
    "1": {"name": "Identified", "count": 0, "leads": []},
    "2": {"name": "Contacted", "count": 0, "leads": []},
    "3": {"name": "Engaged", "count": 0, "leads": []},
    "4": {"name": "Qualified", "count": 0, "leads": []},
    "5": {"name": "Demo/Session", "count": 0, "leads": []},
    "6": {"name": "Proposal", "count": 0, "leads": []},
    "7": {"name": "Closed Won", "count": 0, "leads": []},
    "8": {"name": "Onboarded", "count": 0, "leads": []}
  },
  "leads": [
    {
      "id": "LD-001",
      "company": "Example Corp",
      "website": "https://example.com",
      "contact_name": "Jane Doe",
      "contact_email": "jane@example.com",
      "icp_score": 95,
      "source": "form",
      "stage": 1,
      "status": "new",
      "created_date": "2026-05-01",
      "last_contacted": null,
      "email_sequence_day": 0,
      "notes": "High match — strong ICP fit"
    }
  ]
}
```

**Key fields per lead:**
- `id`: Unique identifier (product-prefix + sequential number)
- `company`, `website`, `contact_name`, `contact_email`: Contact info
- `icp_score`: 0-100 fit score (90+ green, 80-89 yellow, <80 orange)
- `source`: Where the lead came from (form, referral, linkedin, etc.)
- `stage`: 1-8 matching the pipeline stage
- `status`: new, contacted, engaged, qualified, proposed, won, lost
- `email_sequence_day`: Which email in the sequence they're on (0 = not started)
- `last_contacted`: ISO date of last interaction

**Pre-loading leads:** Check for existing prospect lists in `sales/` or `consulting-pipeline/DATA/leads/` to pre-populate pipeline trackers with real prospects.

### STEP 0: Lead Registry & Dedup Discovery

**Purpose:** Maintain a canonical lead registry across all pipeline runs to prevent duplicate processing. Before any lead is added to any pipeline — whether during initial setup, enrichment, or daily orchestrator runs — check the registry first.

**When to trigger:** This is the FIRST step before any pipeline operation (enrichment, email sends, scoring) and the FINAL step after adding any new lead. Always check the registry before creating a new lead entry.

#### Lead Registry File

Create a master registry at `pipeline-engine/data/leads-registry.json`:

```json
{
  "registry_name": "MIFECO Master Lead Registry",
  "description": "Canonical list of all leads ever processed. Used by pipeline orchestrator for deduplication.",
  "last_updated": "ISO-8601",
  "leads": [
    {
      "lead_key": "name|organization|email",
      "source_pipeline": "Books|Consulting|SaaS",
      "original_id": "lead-001",
      "name": "Dr. Sarah Chen",
      "organization": "Northfield Academy",
      "email": "schen@northfieldacademy.edu",
      "current_stage": 3,
      "registered_at": "ISO-8601",
      "status": "active"
    }
  ]
}
```

The `lead_key` is a normalized dedup key: `"name|org|email"` all lowercased and trimmed.

#### Dedup Check Script

Create a CLI tool at `pipeline-engine/data/dedup-check.py` that checks three layers:

```
Layer 1 — Exact match: lead_key (name|org|email) must match exactly → DUPLICATE
Layer 2 — Email match: same email address → DUPLICATE (same person)
Layer 3 — Email domain + name: same email domain AND same contact name → DUPLICATE
         Same company, different person → ALLOW (NOT a duplicate)
```

**Script design:**

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
import json, sys, os

REGISTRY_PATH = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), "leads-registry.json")

def load_registry():
    if os.path.exists(REGISTRY_PATH):
        with open(REGISTRY_PATH) as f:
            return json.load(f)
    return {"leads": []}

def make_key(name, org, email):
    n = (name or "").strip().lower()
    o = (org or "").strip().lower()
    e = (email or "").strip().lower()
    return f"{n}|{o}|{e}"

def check_duplicate(name, org, email):
    key = make_key(name, org, email)
    registry = load_registry()
    for lead in registry["leads"]:
        # L1: Exact key match
        if lead["lead_key"] == key:
            return True, lead
        # L2: Same email
        if email and lead.get("email","").lower() == email.lower():
            return True, lead
        # L3: Same domain + same name
        if email and lead.get("email",""):
            d1 = email.split("@")[-1].lower() if "@" in email else ""
            d2 = lead["email"].split("@")[-1].lower() if "@" in lead.get("email","") else ""
            n1 = (name or "").strip().lower()
            n2 = (lead.get("name","") or "").strip().lower()
            if d1 and d1 == d2 and len(d1) > 3 and n1 and n1 == n2:
                return True, lead
    return False, None
```

**Usage — single lead check:**
```bash
python3 dedup-check.py "John Smith" "Acme Corp" "john@acme.com"
# → {"is_duplicate": false}

python3 dedup-check.py "Rev. Angela Torres" "Hope Fellowship" "atorres@hopefellowship.org"
# → {"is_duplicate": true, "match": {...}}
```

**Usage — batch check (stdin):**
```bash
cat new_leads.json | python3 dedup-check.py
# → {"results": [...], "duplicates_found": 3}
```

#### Integrating into the Pipeline Orchestrator

The daily orchestrator cron job MUST include this as STEP 0:

1. Read `leads-registry.json` to know all previously processed leads
2. For any lead being considered for addition, run `python3 dedup-check.py "<name>" "<org>" "<email>"`
3. If `is_duplicate: true`, SKIP the lead and log it in the daily report
4. After adding new leads, update `leads-registry.json` with new entries

#### Adding Registry Reference to Pipeline Files

Every pipeline JSON file should include a `lead_registry` field:

```json
{
  "lead_registry": {
    "path": "leads-registry.json",
    "dedup_tool": "dedup-check.py",
    "description": "Canonical lead list for dedup across pipeline runs. Run dedup-check.py before adding new leads."
  }
}
```

#### Pitfalls

| Pitfall | Why It Happens | How to Avoid |
|---------|---------------|--------------|
| **False positive on same-company different person** | Org name matches but it's a different contact | Only flag as duplicate when name OR email also matches — not just organization alone. Use Layer 3's domain+name check, not bare org name. |
| **Registry out of sync with pipeline data** | Leads are added to pipeline JSON but not registered | Always update the registry in the same step as adding leads. Make it part of the lead creation workflow. |
| **Registry grows stale** | Dead leads remain in registry forever | Set `status: "active"` initially. When a lead is removed from the pipeline, set `status: "archived"` or `"removed"` rather than deleting — this preserves the dedup check for the same contact in the future. |

#### Pitfall Patching Note

The original skill's synthetic lead removal section (STEP 2.6) says: "When removing synthetic leads from a per-product pipeline JSON, also remove them from the unified pipeline (unified-pipeline.json) if one exists." This is still correct — the registry preserves which leads were removed so they won't be re-added later.

### STEP 2.5: Lead Verification & Enrichment (Operational Run)

**Trigger:** Use this step when the pipeline orchestrator or CEO agent flags leads as needing enrichment — e.g., missing contact names/emails, stale leads stuck in early stages, suspicious-looking opportunities, or after a new lead batch is ingested. This is an **operational run** executed against existing pipeline data, not a one-time setup activity.

**Purpose:** Systematically verify the real-world existence and accuracy of every lead in the pipeline before investing time in outreach. Separate genuine opportunities from placeholder data, dead leads, and potential frauds. Run this across ALL active pipelines (Books, Consulting, SaaS) simultaneously.

#### Search Engine Fallback Strategy

Web research tools frequently fail due to bot detection. Use this fallback chain:

| Priority | Method | Tool | When To Use |
|----------|--------|------|-------------|
| 1 | Browser navigation | `browser_navigate` | Visiting a known company URL directly (e.g., the company's actual website) |
| 2 | Exa API search | `curl` to `api.exa.ai` | High-quality web search — requires API credits |
| 3 | duckduckgo_search Python library | `from duckduckgo_search import DDGS` | When browser and Exa fail due to captchas/rate limits. Already installed in most Hermes environments. |
| 4 | Bing HTML search | `curl` with desktop User-Agent to `bing.com/search` | Last resort — Bing's bot detection is less aggressive than Google/DuckDuckGo |

**DuckDuckGo Search Pattern (preferred fallback, v8.1.1):**
```python
from duckduckgo_search import DDGS
ddgs = DDGS()
results = list(ddgs.text("your search query", max_results=5))
for res in results:
    title = res.get('title','')
    url = res.get('href','')
    body = res.get('body','')
```

Note: DDGS has aggressive rate limiting. On repeated calls, it returns empty results. Interleave queries with pauses or use `delegate_task` for parallel research (each subagent gets its own DDGS instance).

#### Verification Checklist

For each lead, run through this checklist in order (stop at the first strong signal):

| # | Check | Method | What To Look For | Verdict If Failed |
|---|-------|--------|-----------------|-------------------|
| 1 | **Organization website** | Navigate to the organization's claimed URL | Active, real business website with matching description | ⚠️ Flag — dead/parked domain or wrong business |
| 2 | **Email domain** | Check if the domain resolves (browser_navigate or `dig`) | Domain actually serves web content | ⚠️ Flag — unrouteable domain (.edu that doesn't resolve, etc.) |
| 3 | **Google Maps** | Search for the organization name + city | Real physical location or identifiable business | ⚠️ No physical presence found |
| 4 | **Staff/leadership roster** | Navigate to About/Team/Staff/Faculty page | The contact person actually works there | ⚠️ Not on current roster (may be former staff) |
| 5 | **Social media presence** | Check Facebook, LinkedIn, Instagram, etc. | Active, legitimate social media accounts | Minor concern — absence is not disqualifying |
| 6 | **Referral source verification** | Search for the claimed referral source (e.g., "BookExpo 2026") | The event/source actually exists | Minor concern — doesn't validate the lead directly |
| 7 | **Domain registrar status** | For suspicious domains, check if the domain is for sale | The domain is actively used by the business, not parked/listed for sale | 🔴 Major red flag — domain-for-sale = likely dead lead |
| 8 | **Email format validation** | Check if known addresses from the same org follow a consistent pattern | The lead's email follows the org's observed format (e.g., `firstname@org.edu` vs `first.last@org.org`) | ⚠️ Mismatch doesn't disprove the lead but warrants caution |

**Execution pattern:** Use `delegate_task` in parallel (up to 3 at once via `max_concurrent_children`) to research multiple leads simultaneously. Each subagent gets one lead with its specific verification goals.

#### Verification Status Grading

Assign each lead a verification status after research:

| Grade | Meaning | Follow-up Action |
|-------|---------|-----------------|
| ✅ **Confirmed** | Organization verified + contact confirmed on roster/website | Proceed with normal outreach |
| ✅ **Likely Real** | Organization verified, contact not found on roster but email domain matches org pattern | Send outreach — non-response is confirmation |
| ⚠️ **Needs Verification** | Organization exists but contact isn't on roster, email domain format is uncertain | Try alternate email format or call main line |
| ⚠️ **Suspicious** | Domain listed for sale, no physical presence, or inconsistent details | Send a test email — if it bounces, mark as dead |
| 🔴 **Dead** | Email bounces, organization doesn't exist, or all checks fail | Remove from active pipeline |

#### Batch Enrichment Results Update Pattern

After running enrichment on multiple leads (via delegate_task or sequential research), update the pipeline JSON programmatically with ALL enrichment fields, not just notes:

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
import json
from datetime import datetime, timezone

now = datetime.now(timezone.utc).strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ')

enrichment = {
    'C-001': {
        'contact_name': 'Phillip Berry',
        'contact_email': 'pberry@company.com',
        'website': 'company.com',
        'phone': '(555) 123-4567',
        'notes': 'ENRICHED YYYY-MM-DD: Verified real company...',
        'verification_status': 'Confirmed',
        'icp_score': 5,        # 0-10 product fit
        'enriched_at': now,
        'enriched_by': 'agent-enrichment'
    },
    # ... one entry per lead
}

with open('data/pipeline-{product}.json') as f:
    data = json.load(f)

for lead in data['pipeline']['leads']:
    e = enrichment.get(lead['id'])
    if not e:
        continue
    # Update contact fields
    if e.get('contact_name'):
        lead['contact_name'] = e['contact_name']
    if e.get('contact_email'):
        lead['contact_email'] = e['contact_email']
    if e.get('website'):
        lead['website'] = e['website']
    if e.get('phone'):
        lead['phone'] = e['phone']
    # Update metadata
    lead['notes'] = e.get('notes', lead['notes'])
    lead['verification_status'] = e.get('verification_status', 'Unverified')
    lead['icp_score'] = e.get('icp_score', 0)
    lead['enriched_at'] = e.get('enriched_at', now)
    lead['enriched_by'] = e.get('enriched_by', 'agent')
    # Compute rank with hard-gate: no contact = rank 0
    v_lookup = {'Confirmed': 10, 'Likely Real': 7, 'Needs Verification': 3, 'Suspicious': 1, 'Dead': 0, 'Unverified': 1}
    v = v_lookup.get(lead.get('verification_status', 'Unverified'), 0)
    c = 10 if e.get('contact_name') and e.get('contact_email') else (5 if e.get('contact_name') or e.get('contact_email') else 0)
    f = e.get('icp_score', 0)
    # HARD GATE: no contact info = rank 0
    if not e.get('contact_name') or not e.get('contact_email'):
        lead['rank'] = 0
    else:
        lead['rank'] = v + c + f

data['pipeline']['summary']['enriched_leads'] = sum(1 for l in data['pipeline']['leads'] if l.get('enriched_at'))
data['pipeline']['summary']['last_enrichment_run'] = now

with open('data/pipeline-{product}.json', 'w') as f:
    json.dump(data, f, indent=2)
```

This pattern runs automatically after a batch enrichment session. For the `v_lookup` scoring: leads that don't exist on the web get `verification_status='Dead'` → `v=0` → they rank at most 5 (from product fit), pushing them into the 0-4 Dead/Synthetic range.

#### Dead Lead Detection During Enrichment

When researching a lead, if **no registered business entity exists** for the claimed organization name (no website, no business registration, no LinkedIn, no credible directory listing), classify it as **Dead** and remove from the active pipeline:

1. **Exhaustive search:** Run web searches for the exact name + "Inc", "LLC", "Corp", "NGO", "Nonprofit". Check business registries (OpenCorporates, Secretary of State sites), Guidestar for nonprofits, LinkedIn.
2. **Name variation search:** If exact name fails, search stripped-down versions (e.g., "Summit Nonprofit Alliance" → "Summit Nonprofit" → "Summit Alliance").
3. **Confirm dead:** After all searches return no registered entity, mark as `verification_status: "Dead"` and `rank: 0`. Set `status: "removed"` in the pipeline.
4. **Registry preservation:** Keep the lead in `leads-registry.json` with `status: "archived"` so a subsequent enrichment run doesn't re-discover and re-add the same fake lead.
5. **Report:** Log the dead lead in the enrichment report with the search queries used and results found, so a human can verify the decision.

#### Pitfalls

| Pitfall | Why It Happens | How to Avoid |
|---------|---------------|--------------|
| **Confusing "no web presence" with "not real"** | Small/local businesses may have minimal or no website | Check Google Maps + social media. A missing website is not disqualifying for a local business. |
| **Assuming faculty/staff pages are complete** | Schools and small orgs don't always list all staff | Absence from a roster page is suspicious but not definitive. Note it but don't kill the lead on this alone. |
| **Domain-for-sale = dead lead** | Domains can be parked by the owner who still uses the email | The `whois` data may show the same registrant as the claimed business. Test the email address directly. |
| **Treating all leads the same** | Using the same level of verification for a $50 lead as a $6,000 lead | Scale verification effort to deal size. High-value leads (top 20%) get full checklist; low-value leads get checks 1-3 only. |
| **Not updating the pipeline JSON** | Verification is done, notes are in-memory, but the pipeline file stays stale | Always update `notes` and `updated_at` in the pipeline JSON after enrichment so future orchestrator runs have context. |
| **All DuckDuckGo searches returning empty** | Rate limiting — roughly 8 sequential calls triggers empty results; subsequent DDGS instances in the same process also return empty | Use `delegate_task` to run searches in parallel — each subagent gets its own independent DDGS instance with a fresh rate limit. Each subagent should handle 3-5 queries max. If DDGS starts returning empty in the main agent, spawn subagents for remaining queries. Restarting the Python process also resets the rate limit. |

### STEP 2.6: Lead Scoring & Ranking

After verification, score each lead across three dimensions and produce a ranked list across all pipelines. This determines outreach priority.

**Score Components:**

| Dimension | Max Score | What To Measure |
|-----------|-----------|-----------------|
| **Verification** | 10 | ✅ Confirmed=10, ⚠️ Verified partial=5, ❌ Unverified/Synthetic=0 |
| **Contact Availability** | 10 | Valid email+LinkedIn=10, Valid email only=8, Email may work=5, No contact found=0 |
| **Product/Consulting Fit** | 10 | Strong alignment=10, Moderate=5, Weak or unknown=0 |

**Total Score = Verification + Contact + Fit (max 30)**

**⚠️ HARD GATE: No Contact Info = Rank 0**
A lead with a **null/empty contact_name OR null/empty contact_email** has its TOTAL rank set to **0**, regardless of other dimensions. Reasoning: a lead you cannot reach is invisible to the pipeline. The lead must exist in the pipeline JSON (for tracking purposes) but ranks 0 until enriched. This overrides all other score components.

Implementation example:
```python
if not lead.get('contact_name') or not lead.get('contact_email'):
    lead['rank'] = 0
else:
    lead['rank'] = v_score + c_score + f_score
```

**Classification Thresholds:**
| Score | Classification | Action |
|-------|---------------|--------|
| 25+ | 🔥 Hot | Generate outreach (email + LinkedIn + media) immediately |
| 15-24 | Warm | Generate outreach but deprioritize vs hot leads |
| 5-14 | Cold | Send test email to verify before full outreach |
| 1-4 | Dead/Synthetic | Remove from active pipeline or flag for review |
| **0** | **No Contact Info** | **Enrich first — cannot rank/reach** |

**Synthetic Lead Detection:** If a company has no website, no domain that resolves, no Google Maps presence, and no social media — and especially if multiple leads share similar patterns (generic name + unrouteable domain + high ICP score) — flag them as **synthetic/fabricated**. Do NOT send outreach. **IMPORTANT:** When removing synthetic leads from a per-product pipeline JSON, also remove them from the unified pipeline (`unified-pipeline.json`) if one exists — it has its own `leads` array that must stay in sync. The unified pipeline uses prefixed IDs (e.g., `saas-002`), so match on company name or ID number.

### STEP 2.65: Pipeline Date Reset (Fresh Start)

**Trigger conditions:** Use this step when the user says:
- "Reset the pipeline dates" or "reset all task date targets to start from now"
- "No emails have been sent to any leads"
- "Start fresh" with the pipeline
- Pipeline orchestrator is flagging stale dates that have accumulated during setup/testing

**Purpose:** Reset all timestamps across all pipeline data files to the current date, so the orchestrator's stage-threshold logic starts fresh. This is needed when pipeline data was set up/tested with synthetic dates and no real emails have been sent.

**Files to update (all 5):**
```
pipeline-engine/data/
├── pipeline-saas.json       ← Reset created_at + stage + advanced_at
├── pipeline-consulting.json ← Reset created_date + enriched_at + stage
├── pipeline-books.json      ← Reset stage_history + entered_stage + next_action
├── leads-registry.json      ← Update last_updated
└── unified-pipeline.json    ← Reset created_at + last_contact
```

**Pattern for each pipeline:**

**SaaS:** Move all leads back to Stage 1 (Identified), reset `created_at` to now, clear `advanced_at` and `last_auto_advance`.

**Consulting:** Reset `created_date` to today, `enriched_at` to now, move non-dead leads to Stage 1/status=new. Preserve enrichment data and dead lead status.

**Books:** Reset all leads to Stage 1 (Lead Inbox), set `entered_stage` to now, clear `days_in_stage`, set all `stage_history` entries to now with 0 duration. Reset `next_action` and `priority`.

**Registry & Unified:** Update `last_updated` to now. Reset `created_at` and `last_contact` on all unified leads.

**Reference implementation:**

```python
from hermes_tools import terminal, write_file
import json
from datetime import datetime, timezone

base = '/home/bob/.hermes/.openclaw/workspace/pipeline-engine/data'
now = datetime.now(timezone.utc)
today = now.strftime('%Y-%m-%d')
now_iso = now.strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ')

def read_json(path):
    return json.loads(terminal(f'cat {path}', timeout=5)['output'])

# 1. SAAS — reset to Stage 1
saas = read_json(f'{base}/pipeline-saas.json')
for lead in saas['pipeline']['leads']:
    lead['stage'] = 1
    lead['created_at'] = now_iso
    lead['advanced_at'] = None
    lead['notes'] = f"Fresh start {today}. No emails sent."
saas['pipeline']['last_auto_advance'] = None

# 2. CONSULTING — reset dates
consulting = read_json(f'{base}/pipeline-consulting.json')
for lead in consulting['pipeline']['leads']:
    lead['created_date'] = today
    lead['enriched_at'] = now_iso
    if lead.get('verification_status') not in ('Dead',):
        lead['stage'] = 1
        lead['status'] = 'new'
consulting['pipeline']['summary']['last_enrichment_run'] = now_iso

# 3. BOOKS — reset stage histories
books = read_json(f'{base}/pipeline-books.json')
for lead in books['pipeline']['leads']:
    lead['entered_stage'] = now_iso
    lead['days_in_stage'] = 0
    lead['current_stage'] = 1
    lead['current_stage_name'] = 'Lead Inbox'
    for s in lead.get('stage_history', []):
        s['entered'] = now_iso
        s['exited'] = now_iso
        s['duration_days'] = 0
    lead['next_action'] = f"Fresh start {today}."
    lead['priority'] = 'new'
books['pipeline']['metadata']['last_updated'] = now_iso

# 4. REGISTRY
registry = read_json(f'{base}/leads-registry.json')
registry['last_updated'] = now_iso

# 5. UNIFIED
unified = read_json(f'{base}/unified-pipeline.json')
for lead in unified:
    lead['created_at'] = now_iso
    lead['last_contact'] = now_iso
    lead['notes'] = f"Reset {today}. No emails sent."

# Write all files
for fname, data in [('pipeline-saas.json', saas), ('pipeline-consulting.json', consulting),
                     ('pipeline-books.json', books), ('leads-registry.json', registry),
                     ('unified-pipeline.json', unified)]:
    write_file(f'{base}/{fname}', json.dumps(data, indent=2))
```

**⚠️ Pitfalls:**
- **Books stage_history has `exited: null` for current stage** — When resetting, set `exited` to `now_iso` (not null) to make durations computable after reset.
- **Consulting dead leads** — C-005 and C-008 are verified dead. Do NOT change their `verification_status` or `stage` — only update their `created_date`.
- **Registry uses aggregate format** — The `leads-registry.json` may not have a `leads` array with individual entries. If it uses `total_leads_all` and pipeline-grouped counts, only update `last_updated`.
- **timezone-awareness** — All dates should use `datetime.now(timezone.utc)` for ISO format. Avoid tz-naive dates that cause `TypeError` when the orchestrator compares against `datetime.now(timezone.utc)`.

### Nurture Sequence Content Audit & Maintenance

**Trigger:** When the daily pipeline orchestrator flags nurture sequence content discrepancies (wrong product names, wrong book titles, missing catalog items). The orchestrator detects these mismatches and puts email sends ON HOLD — this procedure tells you how to fix them.

**This is a separate workflow from creating sequences from scratch.** The sequences already exist; you're correcting content errors discovered during daily monitoring.

#### Common Discrepancy Patterns

| Pattern | Detection | Root Cause |
|---------|-----------|------------|
| **Wrong book titles** | Books nurture uses "Ignition" but pipeline catalog says "Built from Dust"| Nurture sequence was created before final titles were set |
| **Wrong product names** | SaaS nurture references "LaunchPad" but actual products are Project Hypatia Pro, PM Accelerator, VibraEngineer | Nurture sequence was a generic template, not customized for MIFECO |
| **Missing catalog items** | Pipeline catalog has 7 books, nurture only lists 5 (missing AI That Works for Small Business) | Catalog expanded after nurture was created |
| **Wrong pricing** | Nurture lists $11.99 for a title, pipeline catalog says $9.99 | Prices changed after initial setup |
| **Article prefix variance** | Pipeline says "Oxygen Gamble" but nurture says "The Oxygen Gamble" (same for "Red Charter"/"The Red Charter") | Pipeline uses short/slug titles; nurture uses full display titles with "The" prefix. Decide which is canonical and align both. |

#### Fix Procedure

**1. Load pipeline catalog and nurture sequence side-by-side.**
Read the pipeline JSON data file first (`pipeline-{product}.json` — specifically the `books_available` or key catalog section) and the nurture sequence file (`sequences/{product}-nurture.json`). Compare their data sections for mismatches.

**2. Fix the nurture sequence `books_available` (or product listing) section first.**
Update volume titles, product names, prices, and add missing entries to match the pipeline catalog exactly:

```json
// BEFORE — wrong
{"volume": 1, "title": "No Blue Sky: Ignition", "price": 9.99}

// AFTER — correct
{"volume": 1, "title": "No Blue Sky: Built from Dust", "price": 9.99}
```

**3. Fix ALL email body references.**
For each email in the sequence, search for every occurrence of the old name/title in the `body` field. This includes:
- Catalog/summary sections listing prices or volumes
- Bulk discount examples (e.g., "A Classroom Set of No Blue Sky: Ignition")
- Reader reviews or testimonials that mention specific titles
- Subject lines that reference specific products

Use `patch(mode="replace", path=..., old_string=..., new_string=...)` for each unique string. When the `body` field contains JSON-escaped newlines (`\n`), patch can double-escape them — prefer writing the entire file fresh instead.

**4. Validate JSON integrity.**
```bash
python3 -c "import json; json.load(open('sequences/{product}-nurture.json')); print('✅ Valid')"
```

**5. Verify all copies of wrong names are gone.**
Search the fixed file for the old strings to confirm zero remaining references:
```bash
grep -i "oldtitle\|wrongname" sequences/{product}-nurture.json
# Should return nothing
```

**6. When the fix is complete, the orchestrator's next run will move the held emails from "⏸️ ON HOLD" to "✅ Ready to send".** No manual re-run needed.

#### Full Rebuild vs. Patch

| Scenario | Approach | Example |
|----------|----------|---------|
| Minor title/name changes | Patch individual strings | Books nurture: Ignition→Built from Dust, Ascent→The Oxygen Gamble |
| Complete product mismatch | Full rebuild | SaaS nurture: Entire sequence references a non-existent product "LaunchPad" — every email is wrong |
| Partial mismatch + missing items | Patch + add | Books nurture had wrong titles AND missing AI That Works for Small Business |

**Full rebuild pattern:** When the nurture sequence was built from a generic template for a completely different product line (e.g., "LaunchPad" was a coaching/course platform, but actual MIFECO products are project management tools), the fastest approach is to **write a completely new file** rather than patching individual strings. Create 7 emails covering the actual products:
- Day 1: Suite overview + product matching ("which one fits you?")
- Day 2-4: Deep-dive each product individually
- Day 5: Case studies/real workflows
- Day 6: Transparent pricing
- Day 7: Path-forward options (trial, demo, stay informed)

#### Pitfalls

| Pitfall | Why It Happens | How to Avoid |
|---------|---------------|--------------|
| **Only fixing the catalog section, missing email bodies** | The `books_available` section at the top is obvious; embedded title references in email `body` fields are hidden in long JSON strings | Search every email's `body` for all old title strings. A common miss is the bulk discount example in the final email. |
| **Double-escaped JSON from patch** | The patch tool re-escapes text that already contains escaped newlines (`\n`), producing `\\n` in the JSON string | When a file has JSON with embedded `\n` (newline escape sequences), write the entire file fresh instead of patching individual strings within body fields |
| **Forgetting to add missing products** | Only the titles that changed get attention; products added since the nurture was created go unnoticed | Always compare the nurture's `books_available` against the pipeline catalog's `books_available` — add any that are missing |

Create a daily cron job that monitors pipeline health:

```bash
  schedule="0 8 * * *" \
```

#### STEP 6.1: What the Daily Cron Does

The daily pipeline orchestrator cron job performs the following operations in order:

**STEP 0: Dedup Discovery Check**
1. Read `leads-registry.json` to know all previously processed leads
2. For any NEW lead being considered for addition, run `python3 data/dedup-check.py "<name>" "<org>" "<email>"`
3. If `is_duplicate: true`, SKIP the lead and log it in the daily report
4. If a lead appears in a pipeline JSON but is NOT in the registry, re-register it
5. Verify registry lead count matches total leads across all pipeline files

**STEP 1: Read All Pipeline Data**
- Read each pipeline JSON: `pipeline-saas.json`, `pipeline-consulting.json`, `pipeline-books.json`
- Read each nurture sequence: `sequences/saas-nurture.json`, `sequences/consulting-nurture.json`, `sequences/books-nurture.json`
- Read the master lead registry: `leads-registry.json`
- Read any unified pipeline: `unified-pipeline.json`

**STEP 2: Calculate Days-in-Stage (per pipeline)**

For each lead, determine when they entered their CURRENT stage:

```python
def stage_entry_time(lead, stage_num):
    # 1. Check stage_history for an entry matching current stage
    for entry in lead.get('stage_history', []):
        if entry.get('stage_id') == stage_num:
            return entry.get('entered_at')
    # 2. If not found, use exit time of PREVIOUS stage
    prev_stage = stage_num - 1
    for entry in lead.get('stage_history', []):
        if entry.get('stage_id') == prev_stage:
            return entry.get('exited_at')
    # 3. Fallback to created_at
    return lead.get('created_at')
```

**Critical:** Do NOT fall through to `created_at` for leads that have a stage_history with previous stage exits — the exit of the previous stage IS the entry of the current stage. Using `created_at` overestimates days-in-stage.

**⚠️ Timezone pitfall:** Pipeline data may mix tz-aware dates (`"2026-04-28T00:00:00Z"`) with tz-naive date-only fields (`"created_date": "2026-04-20"`). When comparing against `datetime.now(timezone.utc)`, Python raises `TypeError: can't subtract offset-naive and offset-aware datetimes`. Always normalize: parse to offset-aware if Z/offset present, otherwise treat as UTC-relative:

```python
from datetime import datetime, timezone
def parse_date(s):
    dt = datetime.fromisoformat(s.replace("Z", "+00:00"))
    if dt.tzinfo is None:
        dt = dt.replace(tzinfo=timezone.utc)
    return dt
```

### STEP 10.3: Email Enrichment Gate — Block Unsafe Sends

**Trigger conditions:** Use this procedure when the content command center has nurture sequence emails with template placeholders (`{{email}}`, `{{name}}`) instead of real recipient addresses, and you need to prevent them from appearing as sendable.

**Class:** "Enforcing email validation gate in content command center dashboards — no email without a real `to:` address should reach the sendable viewer."

#### The Problem

Nurture sequence emails are templates — they use `{{email}}`, `{{name}}`, `{{company}}` placeholders. If these appear in the EMAILS viewer alongside emails with real `to:` addresses (e.g., `alice@testcorp.com`), a user could accidentally try to send a template without lead data and get a bounced/silently-failed email.

#### The Fix Pattern

1. **Split EMAILS into two arrays:**
   - `EMAILS` — only items with valid `to:` addresses (real emails like `user@domain.com`)
   - `EMAIL_TEMPLATES` — items with placeholder `to:` fields, marked as `NEEDS_ENRICHMENT`

2. **Add a separate Enrichment viewer tab** that displays templates needing enrichment:
   - Shows the `NEEDS_ENRICHMENT` badge prominently
   - Warns the user that pairing with a lead is required before sending
   - Filters by pipeline and text search

3. **Add client-side email validation** before sending:
   - `isValidEmail()` — regex check for valid email format
   - `getEmailFromToField()` — extract email from `"Name <email>"` or bare `"email"` format
   - In `sendEmailForReal()`, validate the `to:` field and block with an alert if no real email found

4. **Template state model:**
   ```javascript
   // EMAIL_TEMPLATES — each has to: 'NEEDS_ENRICHMENT'
   {id:'em1',pipeline:'SaaS',day:1,from:'Sender <sender@domain.com>',to:'NEEDS_ENRICHMENT',subject:'Welcome {{name}}',body:'Hi {{name}}...',cta:'Reply'}
   
   // After enrichment — moved to EMAILS with real address
   {id:'em1',pipeline:'SaaS',day:1,from:'Sender <sender@domain.com>',to:'John Doe <john@company.com>',subject:'Welcome John!',body:'Hi John...',cta:'Reply'}
   ```

5. **Render difference:** The `renderEmails()` function only displays items from `EMAILS`. Templates in `EMAIL_TEMPLATES` go to a separate `renderEnrichmentQueue()` function.

6. **Enrichment workflow:**
   - Look up matching leads from pipeline JSON data that have `contact_email` fields
   - Replace `{{name}}` and `{{email}}` with actual lead data
   - Update `to:` from `NEEDS_ENRICHMENT` to the real recipient
   - Move the enriched item from `EMAIL_TEMPLATES` to `EMAILS`

#### The Multi-File Update Pattern

Every product change requires updates in this order:

```
1. PIPELINE DATA JSON  → 2. NURTURE SEQUENCE JSON  → 3. DASHBOARD HTML  → 4. COMMAND CENTER HTML
(pipeline-{product}.json)  (sequences/{product}-nurture.json)  (pipeline-dashboard.html)  (content-command-center.html)
```

**Why this order:** Data files are the source of truth. Sequences reference them. Dashboards display them. Command centers embed their email content. Going in order prevents forward-referencing errors.

| Pitfall | Why It Happens | How to Avoid |
|---------|---------------|--------------|
| **Updating dashboard but not data files** | Dashboard HTML has embedded JS arrays; JSON data files power cron orchestrator | Always update BOTH the JSON data file AND the dashboard's embedded JS data array |
| **Forgetting the overview card tags** | Consulting overview card has separate tag badges that don't auto-update | Search for `<span class="tag">` near the consulting overview card and update |

| **Breaking JSON with patch escape issues** | Patch can double-escape `\n` in JSON body fields | For JSON with embedded newline escapes, write the entire file fresh instead of patching within body fields |
| **Leaving old grid columns in HTML** | Grid CSS remains at old column count | Update `grid-template-columns:repeat(3,1fr)` to match new tier count |

## Pitfalls

1. **Don't skip the architecture doc.** Without it, the pipeline structure is implicit and will be inconsistent across product lines. Write ARCHITECTURE.md first.
2. **Use AgentMail, not SendGrid/Postmark.** AgentMail auto-generates inboxes and is already configured. Don't waste time setting up email services — the forms POST to AgentMail's API. Actual email sending requires AgentMail's send API or manual sending.
